raw_text: Nepal and China on Monday signed a framework agreement for the long-discussed trans-Himalayan railway that would connect Kerung in Tibet to Kathmandu. The project is estimated to cost USD 3.5 billion, with China providing the bulk of financing through concessional loans. The railway would traverse some of the most challenging terrain on earth, crossing the Himalayan range at altitudes exceeding 4,000 metres. Indian analysts have flagged the project's potential dual-use implications for military logistics.
clean_text: Nepal-China signed trans-Himalayan railway agreement connecting Kerung to Kathmandu. USD 3.5B Chinese financing. Railway crosses Himalayas above 4000m. India flags dual-use concerns.
